correctness.rationale: Every relative payoff order has probability 1/9!, and every order has exactly one candidate row-minimum/column-maximum map. The nine-element linear-extension recurrence counts each map without omission or overlap; its 729 weighted map totals sum to 362880. The independent brute-force enumerator visits every one of those 362880 permutations, obtaining the same eight cycle/max-depth counts and five vertex-depth counts; the results total 6*9! for rooted starts. A separate 72*96 maximal-chain calculation and explicit matrix witness certify the sharp tail. Theorem scope is finite and complete, not an infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The nearest source, Karelas–Lugosi–Zhang (2026), analyzes the same zero-sum best-response graph but the inspected Section 6 addresses cycle probabilities and asymptotic cycle statistics; it does not state or imply the entry-time law from only those cycle counts. Its path-length theorem in Section 5 assumes B=A, not B=-A. Heinrich et al. (2023) use a distinct payoff-dependence model. Exact literature and result searches under transient/absorption/preperiod aliases found no stronger coverage. Unindexed equivalent finite enumerations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact time until deterministic alternating best-response dynamics enter a recurrent class is a natural algorithmic and game-dynamical observable, and it cannot be reconstructed from the previously treated cycle count. The first square zero-sum size with a four-edge transient is three strategies per side; the complete hitting-time law, its distribution-free mean 179/315, and the sharp delay frequency 2/105 form a full natural finite classification. The result is motivated by the literature on cycle structure and has uses as a finite-game calibration benchmark without requiring an unproved downstream theorem.
